title: Indoor Air Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor return-air thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription:
Error CH01 on LG mini-splits indicates a fault with the indoor room temperature sensor. This thermistor measures return-air temperature used for setpoint control.

The most common issue is a loose connector on the indoor PCB. Replacement sensors are inexpensive and widely available via LG parts distributors.

After replacing, power cycle the unit to clear the error history.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before opening indoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open indoor unit and firmly reseat the thermistor plug on PCB.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if fault persists after sensor replacement.

faq.a: At the return-air inlet inside the indoor unit.

title: Indoor Pipe Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor coil inlet pipe thermistor is faulty.
fullDescription:
Error CH02 indicates the indoor heat exchanger inlet pipe temperature sensor is open, shorted, or reporting invalid values. This sensor is used for freeze protection and mode control.

Verify connector seating, then test sensor resistance. Replacement is straightforward.

faq.a: The liquid inlet pipe on indoor coil.

title: Remote Controller Communication Error
shortDescription: Communication between remote controller and indoor unit has failed.
fullDescription:
Error CH03 indicates the wired remote controller cannot communicate with the indoor unit. Check the controller cable connections and integrity. Wireless remotes are not affected by CH03.

Reseat the controller cable at both ends; many CH03 errors resolve with a firm connection.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Check connections at controller and indoor PCB.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if controller or PCB needs replacement.

title: Drain Pump / Float Switch Fault
shortDescription: The drain system has tripped or failed.
fullDescription:
Error CH04 indicates the drain float switch has tripped or the drain pump has failed. Water is backing up in the pan and cooling is disabled to prevent overflow damage.

Clear the condensate line first - this is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Test pump
fixSteps.instruction: Pour water in pan and verify pump activates.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if pump replacement needed.

title: Indoor-Outdoor Communication Error
shortDescription: Communication between indoor and outdoor units failed.
fullDescription:
Error CH05 indicates indoor and outdoor units are not communicating. Check signal wire polarity, terminal tightness, and outdoor power.

LG communication is polarity-sensitive on some models - verify wiring matches the installation diagram.

fixSteps.title: Tighten terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat signal wires at both units.

fixSteps.title: Verify polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Match wire numbers to installation diagram.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if PCB fault suspected.

faq.a: Typically wire 3 or marked 'S' - verify with installation manual.

title: Indoor Outlet Pipe Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor coil outlet pipe thermistor is faulty.
fullDescription:
Error CH06 indicates the outlet-side pipe sensor on the indoor heat exchanger is out of range. This sensor works with CH02 for superheat/subcool control.

Replacement is straightforward with OEM part.

faq.a: Gas line exiting the indoor coil.

title: Indoor EEPROM Error
shortDescription: Indoor PCB memory chip fault or corruption.
fullDescription:
Error CH09 indicates the indoor unit PCB EEPROM (non-volatile memory) has a read/write fault or data corruption. Typically requires PCB replacement.

Power cycling may clear transient faults. Persistent CH09 needs PCB replacement.

faq.a: Not in the field; PCB replacement is standard.

title: Indoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor fan motor is locked, overloaded, or has lost feedback.
fullDescription:
Error CH10 indicates the indoor fan motor is not operating correctly. Causes include seized bearings, obstructed blower wheel, damaged Hall sensor wiring, or a failed motor.

Clean the blower wheel first - accumulated dust often causes overcurrent conditions.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power and ensure blades have stopped.

faq.a: Modern LG units use DC variable-speed motors.

title: Indoor Discharge Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor discharge/supply air sensor is faulty.
fullDescription:
Error CH12 indicates the indoor supply air (discharge) temperature sensor is out of range. This sensor measures the air leaving the coil and is used for comfort control and delta-T monitoring.

Verify connector and test resistance before replacing.

faq.a: No - discharge is air leaving coil, return is air entering.

title: Outdoor IPM / Compressor DC Peak
shortDescription: Inverter power module detected excessive DC current to compressor.
fullDescription:
Error CH21 indicates the outdoor IPM (intelligent power module) detected a DC peak current fault. This may be from a shorted compressor winding, failed IPM transistor, or overvoltage event.

This is a serious fault requiring professional diagnosis. Repeated restart attempts will damage the PCB further.
safetyWarning: Lethal voltages. Let capacitors discharge 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Do not reset repeatedly
fixSteps.instruction: Stop attempts to avoid PCB damage.

fixSteps.title: Test compressor windings
fixSteps.instruction: Pro to verify isolation and balance.

faq.a: Yes, recommended to prevent repeat failures.

title: Outdoor Compressor Overcurrent
shortDescription: Compressor current exceeded safe operating limit.
fullDescription:
Error CH22 indicates the compressor drew excessive AC current. Causes include dirty outdoor coil, refrigerant overcharge, blocked condenser airflow, or a failing compressor.

Clean outdoor coil and verify fan operation before calling for refrigerant diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Clean coil
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse outdoor fins with garden hose.

fixSteps.title: Verify fan
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure outdoor fan runs at full speed.

whenToCallPro: Call pro for refrigerant or compressor diagnosis.

title: Outdoor DC Link Low Voltage
shortDescription: DC bus voltage in outdoor inverter fell below safe level.
fullDescription:
Error CH23 indicates the DC link voltage on the outdoor PCB is below threshold. Causes include low line voltage, failed rectifier, or a bad DC bus capacitor.

Measure supply voltage first; if line voltage is adequate, PCB diagnosis is needed.
safetyWarning: Lethal DC voltages on bus capacitors.

faq.a: Ask utility if brownouts are common in area.

title: Outdoor Compressor Position / DC Error
shortDescription: Inverter lost compressor rotor position feedback.
fullDescription:
Error CH26 indicates the sensorless position estimation for the compressor failed. Often caused by rapid load changes, failing IPM, or compressor winding imbalance.

Professional service is required.

title: PSC (Power Source Circuit) Error
shortDescription: Error in the outdoor power source or PFC circuit.
fullDescription:
Error CH27 indicates a fault in the PSC/PFC (power factor correction) circuit on the outdoor PCB. This affects how the unit draws AC power and converts it to DC for the inverter.

PCB replacement is typically required.

faq.a: Power factor correction - improves efficiency of AC to DC conversion.

title: Inverter Compressor Overcurrent
shortDescription: DC current to compressor exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription:
Error CH29 indicates an overcurrent condition on the DC side of the inverter to compressor. Similar root causes to CH22 but measured at the inverter output.

Dirty outdoor coil is the most common DIY-addressable cause.

causes.cause: Dirty outdoor coil / poor heat rejection

fixSteps.title: Verify airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure no obstructions around outdoor unit.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if cleaning does not resolve.

faq.a: Minimum 2 ft on sides, 5 ft on intake and discharge.

fullDescription: On a multi-zone system, indoor units cannot run different modes (e.g. heat vs cool). Set all indoor units to the same mode.

fixSteps.instruction: Replace identified faulty sensor or motor.

whenToCallPro: Sealed system or inverter PCB diagnostics require an LG-trained technician.

title: Indoor Reverse Phase
fullDescription: On 3-phase systems, the phase rotation is reversed and must be corrected for the compressor to operate safely.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: CH19 shown on display or remote
Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is integrated to PCB.

faq.a: Vibration loosens the plug over time.

safetyWarning: Cap on inverter PCB; verify discharge before touching.

title: Suction Pipe Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Suction line temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription: CH46 indicates the suction temperature sensor at the outdoor unit failed, preventing accurate superheat calculation.

fixSteps.title: Locate sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor clamps to suction pipe inside outdoor unit.

whenToCallPro: If sensor wires are damaged near the pipe.

title: Compressor Discharge Pipe Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Discharge pipe sensor at the compressor is faulty.
fullDescription: CH47 indicates the discharge thermistor is open or shorted, removing high-temp protection.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wire
fixSteps.instruction: Look for melted insulation near compressor.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor with high-temp sleeve.

safetyWarning: Compressor body extremely hot during operation.
